title: Ra's secret name: how Isis stole the sun god's power

scenes.text: Egypt's mightiest god had one weak spot: his name. And a goddess stole it.
Ra says it himself: I am Khepera in the morning, Ra at noon, and Temu in the evening.
But his secret name was hidden inside his body by his father and mother, so that no spell could master him.
Isis knew words of power, and she wanted to be as great as Ra.
She takes the old god's spittle, kneads it with dust… and makes a serpent.
She lays it on his path. It bites him, and the living fire leaves his body.
Isis only heals him once Ra lets his name pass from his body into hers.
Then she speaks the spell: flow, poison! Ra lives! The poison dies!
Ever since, Isis is the Queen of the gods, who knows Ra by his own name.
Which text says so? An Egyptian papyrus kept in Turin.
Save it, and send it to anyone who thinks Ra was invincible.
